ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD\perp BC$ and $CE\perp AB$ with perpendicular feet at points D and E respectively, $AD$ and $CE$ intersect at point H, and $AE=CE$. Since $\triangle BEC\cong \triangle HEA$, if $BE=8$ and $CH=3$, what is the length of the line segment $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: From Equation (1), we know that $\triangle BEC \cong \triangle HEA$,\\
hence, BE = EH = 8,\\
since CH = 3,\\
thus, CE = AE = 3 + 8 = 11,\\
therefore, AB = AE + BE = 11 + 8 = \boxed{19}.

Since $\triangle BEC\cong \triangle HEA$, if $BE=8$ and $CH=3$, what is the length of the line segment $AB$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC, with B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and A above; point E is located on line segment BA, CE is perpendicular to AB and has a right-angle mark; point D is located on BC, AD is perpendicular to BC and has a right-angle mark; line segments AD and CE intersect at H, and from the figure it can be seen that H is on line segment CE and is between C and E, and E is on line segment AB and is between B and A. Reasoning: According to the given congruence order △BEC ≅ △HEA, the corresponding points are B ↔ H, E ↔ E, C ↔ A, so the corresponding side BE = HE. Given BE = 8, so HE = 8. Also given CH = 3, and H is between C and E, so CE = CH + HE = 3 + 8 = 11. By corresponding sides there is also CE = EA, so EA = 11. Because E is between B and A, AB = BE + EA = 8 + 11 = 19.
